relationship.statement: A pendulum's swing period grows as the square root of string length and shrinks with stronger gravity, while bob mass cancels out. Release angle sets swing width and peak speed, and slightly lengthens the period once swings are no longer small.
assumptions: Air drag, pivot friction, and string mass are neglected.
The pendulum bob acts as a point mass on a taut, inextensible line.
Small swing angles (sin θ ≈ θ) are assumed for the simple period law.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the fixed pivot point to the bob's center of mass.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration pulling the bob toward equilibrium.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the pendulum bob; increases weight and inertia equally.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle measured from straight down where the bob is released.

quantities.label: Swing period
quantities.meaning: Exact time for one complete back-and-forth swing at any release angle.

quantities.label: Small-angle period
quantities.meaning: Ideal period 2π√(L/g) when sin θ ≈ θ, ignoring release angle.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest vertical point.

quantities.label: Restoring force
quantities.meaning: Tangential force m·g·sin(θ₀) pulling the bob back at release.

quantities.label: Restoring accel.
quantities.meaning: Tangential acceleration g·sin(θ₀) at release; bob mass cancels out.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = 1.5; var m = 2.0; var g = inputs.gravity; var theta0Deg = inputs.start_angle; var theta0 = theta0Deg * Math.PI / 180; var half0 = 0.5 * theta0; var k = Math.sin(half0); var omega0 = Math.sqrt(g / L); var smallPeriod = 2 * Math.PI / omega0; var N = 6; var a = new Array(N + 1); var c = new Array(N + 1); a[0] = 1; var b = Math.cos(half0); c[0] = k; for (var i = 0; i < N; i++) { a[i + 1] = 0.5 * (a[i] + b); c[i + 1] = 0.5 * (a[i] - b); b = Math.sqrt(a[i] * b); } var agm = a[N]; var K = 0.5 * Math.PI / agm; var exactPeriod = smallPeriod / agm; var w = (omega0 * t + K) % (4 * K); var phi = Math.pow(2, N) * agm * w; for (var j = N; j >= 1; j--) { phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin((c[j] / a[j]) * Math.sin(phi))); } var sinHalf = k * Math.sin(phi); if (sinHalf > 1) { sinHalf = 1; } if (sinHalf < -1) { sinHalf = -1; } var theta = 2 * Math.asin(sinHalf); var thetaIdeal = theta0 * Math.cos(omega0 * t); var bobX = L * Math.sin(theta); var bobY = -L * Math.cos(theta); var idealX = L * Math.sin(thetaIdeal); var idealY = -L * Math.cos(thetaIdeal); var sin0 = Math.sin(theta0); var cos0 = Math.cos(theta0); var startX = L * sin0; var startY = -L * cos0; var maxSpeed = 2 * Math.sqrt(g * L) * k; var restoringAccel = g * sin0; var restoringForce = m * restoringAccel; var gravArrowLen = 0.12 + 0.018 * g; var gravTipY = bobY - gravArrowLen; var restArrowLen = 0.08 + 0.024 * restoringAccel; var restTipX = startX - restArrowLen * cos0; var restTipY = startY - restArrowLen * sin0; var vmaxTipX = 0.08 + 0.065 * maxSpeed; return { period: exactPeriod, small_angle_period: smallPeriod, max_speed: maxSpeed, restoring_force: restoringForce, restoring_accel: restoringAccel, bob_x: bobX, bob_y: bobY, ideal_x: idealX, ideal_y: idealY, start_x: startX, start_y: startY, grav_tip_y: gravTipY, rest_tip_x: restTipX, rest_tip_y: restTipY, vmax_tip_x: vmaxTipX, angle_deg: theta * 180 / Math.PI, ideal_angle_deg: thetaIdeal * 180 / Math.PI, is_small_angle: theta0Deg <= 20, is_large_angle: theta0Deg >= 45, is_weak_gravity: g < 5, is_strong_gravity: g > 15 }; }

cases.text: Small angle: exact matches ideal T
Wide swing: exact T lags ideal T
Weak g slows swing and lowers vmax
Strong g speeds up swing and vmax

explanation.otherwise: Mid angle: slight lag vs ideal T

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Watch an exact pendulum swing beside an ideal small-angle model with length and mass fixed. Adjust gravity and release angle to see how period, peak speed, and phase lag change.
lesson.instructions: Drag Gravity to compare weak and strong downward pull, and drag Release angle to test small swings against wide swings. Pause or scrub time to inspect the gap between the exact bob and the small-angle reference.
lesson.goal: Stronger gravity shortens the swing period and raises peak speed, while bob mass cancels out; wider release angles boost speed and restoring pull and slightly lengthen the true period.
